videos.title: Not all bird feeders work for all birds, and that matters most during fall migration. Clinging birds
videos.description:
Not all bird feeders work for all birds, and that matters most during fall migration. Clinging birds like woodpeckers, nuthatches, and chickadees use their feet and tail to grip while feeding, making suet or mesh feeders (filled with peanuts or a fruit and nut mix) their best option. Perching birds like cardinals, sparrows, doves, and finches prefer to sit and eat, so a standard seed feeder with a perch is ideal. Combination feeders accommodate both styles at once, an easy way to attract more species to your yard as birds fuel up for the season ahead.

videos.title: Molting season is here, and it explains why your backyard birds look a little scruffy! Birds shed ol
videos.description:
Molting season is here, and it explains why your backyard birds look a little scruffy! Birds shed old, worn feathers and grow new ones this time of year, which takes a lot of energy. That means they need extra protein: peanuts, suet, mealworms, and high protein seed blends are all great choices. Placing feeders near trees or bushes also gives molting birds a safe place to hide, since they can't fly from predators as quickly while regrowing feathers.

videos.title: I filmed a hummingbird "acting confused" at a sunflower while on vacation in Granby, Colorado, but i
videos.description:
I filmed a hummingbird "acting confused" at a sunflower while on vacation in Granby, Colorado, but it turns out this is completely normal hummingbird feeding behavior! Sunflower centers are made up of hundreds of tiny disc florets that open in rings over several days, and hummingbirds also hunt small insects hiding in the florets, especially heading into migration season. Watch him work the whole flower center in this short clip!

videos.title: Busting the biggest hummingbird migration myth right now 🐦
videos.description:
Busting the biggest hummingbird migration myth right now 🐦

Leaving your feeder out too long will NOT trick hummingbirds into staying, their migration instinct is way stronger than that. But here's what actually helps them on their journey south: keep feeders out 1-2 weeks after your last sighting (aim for around October 15th or after the second freeze), clean every 5-7 days (sooner if the nectar looks cloudy), and use a 4:1 water-to-sugar ratio for homemade nectar or grab our Petal Potion for a ready-made option. Dealing with bees or ants? An all-natural bee spray and a simple ant moat solve both problems. And if you're due for a feeder upgrade, ceramic feeders naturally shade the nectar so it lasts longer with less work for you.

videos.title: Vacationing in Granby, Colorado this week and doing plenty of birding while I'm here! One bird kept
videos.description:
Vacationing in Granby, Colorado this week and doing plenty of birding while I'm here! One bird kept singing from a riverside bush and stumped my Merlin app for days. When I finally got him on video and uploaded a photo, Merlin identified him as a Western Flycatcher, a bird with some behaviors similar to our Eastern Phoebe back home in Omaha, but a completely different species suited to a completely different part of the country. Such a fun reminder of how much your local bird list changes with the landscape.
